title: Flag scores outside the reliable range
statement: Find the ability range over which a test measures reliably, flag every score outside it, and send students below its floor to an instrument built for them.
example: One adaptive reading test measured reliably from 160 to 230 on its score scale, with reliability of at least 0.85, and planned to route readers below its floor to a lower-grade test.
detail: A reading assessment's floor-and-ceiling simulation defines its reliable range as the abilities where reliability reaches 0.85, citing the testing standards' requirement to document the score range within which valid inferences can be made; on the full bank that range ran from RIT 160 to 230. Its score reports carry an above, within or below reliable-range flag, and students below the bank's floor are to go to the official lower-grade instrument rather than be measured past it. At the top, the package added harder items instead.
against: The routing was asserted before it was built: "Below-floor students "route to official K–2 MAP" — a handoff that is asserted, not built (who routes, and how?)." (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md`, line 58). The documents also disagree on the cut: RIT 155 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/MAP_PROXY_VALIDITY_CASE.md`, line 147) against the simulated reliable floor of RIT 160, with "only the bottom ~5% of readers (below RIT 160) route to the K–2 MAP instrument" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`, line 44).

evidence.quote: Statistical basis: characterizing floor and ceiling is required under AERA/APA/NCME Standards §4.9 [AERA-2014] to document the score range within which valid inferences can be made.
Reliable range defined as: reliability ≥ 0.85 at that theta level
